seed: Battery, Graphite stage A (launch conditions and host fragility). Cooling and motor have no stage A yet.
rules: cause and fix_ref are taken only from cited records; time_lost is UNKNOWN unless a record states it
no spend figure, balance or account detail is recorded here; rates and caps live in the grant files
rank orders the automation backlog by expected time saved on the NEXT Challenge: how often it recurs at a wave start, and whether a tool already prevents it; hours stay UNKNOWN until measured

blockers.name: Wrong lane
blockers.cause: A run was launched against a lane (signer, Control Center, tunnels) other than the one the run needed. Hotkeys are bound to one deployment: minerD-G stay on main for L0 confirmations, the ladder uses its own hotkeys.
blockers.occurrences: AT_LEAST_1 (stage A failed four times on launch conditions, of which this is one)
blockers.fix_ref: GRAPHITE-LAUNCH-PREFLIGHT-01 (#967): lane endpoint and tunnel checks; the probe has not run against the live account

automation.what: Generate the lane file from the lane registry (lane name to signer, Control Center, tunnels, key paths) instead of hand-writing it per wave.

blockers.name: Keys in the wrong distro
blockers.cause: Key files the launch needed were in a different WSL distro or path than the one running the executor.
cause_source: docs/development/evidence/launchpad-acceptance-2026-10-07/FINDINGS.md (LA-F6: a fresh distro lacks what the service needs; related, not the same fault)
blockers.fix_ref: GRAPHITE-LAUNCH-PREFLIGHT-01 (#967): every key file must exist with mode 600, checked by path only; no key is read

automation.what: The wave template names key slots (not paths) and the preflight reports the missing ones together as owner_needs.

blockers.name: One controller per root
blockers.cause: Two runs shared one controller root. The controller counts every run and binds one grant document, and the wave plan requires one root per run.
blockers.fix_ref: GRAPHITE-LAUNCH-PREFLIGHT-01 (#967): roots distinct, not nested, outside the repository, no more than the grant's max_concurrency

automation.what: The wave template allocates one fresh root per planned concurrent run and prints the --root list for the preflight.

blockers.name: Pod ceiling below the offered price
blockers.cause: Pods were refused at launch. The rate in the grant is a ceiling and the runner refuses a pod RunPod offers above it.
cause_source: Test Lead note to the Graphite Testing Manager, 2026-10-10 (stage A first launch refused pods)
blockers.occurrences: 1 live: the stage A first launch failed on pod refusal because the grant's rate ceiling was below the offered price of the GPU class (Test Lead note, 2026-10-10)
blockers.fix_ref: PR 969 (GRANT-POD-CEILING-01) makes the pod rate ceiling a grant field and the owner approved a standing ceiling and token share; the figures are in that decision record, not repeated here. The relaunch waits on 969 merging. The preflight --probe (#967) detects the mismatch but did not run against the live account before the launch.

automation.what: The wave template runs the probe before proposing a grant and states the observed offer against the proposed rate ceiling, so the proposal carries a ceiling that can launch. The proposal is the owner's to approve; nothing is authored as spend.

blockers.name: Token share and pod split
blockers.cause: A run's worst case is split between tokens and pods. With a large start model, one full-window call reserves more than the token share, so a session stops before its first call (D35 for the kimi-k3 Attacker under the phase 4 grant).
cause_source: Test Lead note to the Graphite Testing Manager, 2026-10-10 (token share approved alongside the pod ceiling in PR 969)
blockers.occurrences: 2: found in planning (D35), and the stage A first launch also needed a different token share (Test Lead note, 2026-10-10)
blockers.fix_ref: PR 969 carries the owner-approved standing token share for the stage grants. Still OPEN: no check refuses a grant whose split cannot fund one full-window call of the start model, or whose pod share cannot fund the pods at the rate ceiling.

automation.what: The wave template computes the split from the model's full-window reservation and pods x rate ceiling, and the preflight refuses a grant whose split fails either.

blockers.name: Reboot fragility
blockers.cause: After a host reboot the signers and the tunnels the lanes need were down, so the lanes could not be confirmed ready until the owner restarted both.
cause_source: Launchpad note to the Graphite Testing Manager, 2026-10-10 (signers and tunnels down since the reboot; owner restarting)
docs/development/graphite/GRAPHITE_LADDER_STAGE_A_CHECKLIST.md (precondition 5: lane checked after the WSL restart)
docs/development/graphite/LAUNCH_PREFLIGHT.md (run before every launch and after any restart)
blockers.fix_ref: The preflight detects the state after a restart. Nothing brings the signers and tunnels back up, and a signer start stays a human act (miner-setup rule).

automation.what: One lane-up command per lane that lists what is down, prints the single owner action to restore it, and re-runs the preflight when the owner says it is done. It never starts a signer or signs.

blockers.name: Auto-mode permission blocks
blockers.cause: Agent sessions in auto mode had edits blocked by the permission classifier, for at least one class of edit (the signer auto-confirm build, per the cited decision).
cause_source: .agent/decisions/2026-10-08-OWNER-CANARY-MINER-01.md (SIGNER-AUTOCONFIRM-01 build blocked by the auto-mode permission classifier)
blockers.occurrences: AT_LEAST_1 (signer auto-confirm build, per the cited decision); other edit classes (for example GPU allocation and cleanup) are reported in session notes that are not in the repository, so they are not counted here
blockers.fix_ref: None in code. The workaround is the owner switching that session to approve-edits mode. Which edit classes trigger the block is not recorded in one place.

automation.what: The wave template lists the edit classes known to need approve-edits mode, so the owner is asked once, in the same batched question as the wave's other owner needs, before the session starts.

blockers.name: Silent failures
blockers.cause: A live run could stall, or every pod launch could be refused, with nothing visible to the coordinator until someone looked.
blockers.fix_ref: GRAPHITE-LAUNCH-PREFLIGHT-01 (#967): a heartbeat every 2 minutes; STALLED when it is more than 15 minutes old while the run is alive, or when every pod launch was refused

automation.what: A collector that reads the shared heartbeat directory and raises one line to the coordinator when a run reads STALLED, so a stall is announced rather than found.

blockers.name: Lane install lagging the grant code
blockers.cause: The lane install code lagged behind the grant code, so a lane refused a current grant with grant_exact_fields_required.
cause_source: Test Lead note to the Graphite Testing Manager, 2026-10-10 (stage A)
blockers.fix_ref: Decided: Launchpad is the single owner of lane installs. Proposed, not built: a preflight check that the lane revision equals the grant's code revision. The existing preflight check compares the checkout HEAD with the profile's accepted_revision (carbon/agent_campaign/graphite/preflight.py), which is a different comparison.

automation.what: Preflight refuses a launch when the lane's installed revision differs from the revision the grant's code is at, and names the lane owner to reinstall.

blockers.name: One shared checkout for every lane
blockers.cause: carbon-fresh has one shared checkout, so two sessions updating it collided and every lane's profile went stale (carbon_updated_rerun_installer).
cause_source: Test Lead note to the Graphite Testing Manager, 2026-10-10 (stage A)
blockers.fix_ref: Decided: Launchpad is the single owner of lane installs, so only one session updates the shared checkout. No code enforces the single owner; the proposed revision-equality check (B9) would detect the stale profile.

automation.what: The wave template names the one lane-install owner and the lane-up command (B6) runs the installer, so no other session updates the shared checkout.

ask_owning_sessions.one_batched_question: For each of B1-B8, give the time lost in stage A (hours or UNKNOWN), the number of occurrences, and whether the fix has been exercised live; and name the edit classes the auto-mode classifier blocked (B7).
